query: If we add dyadic partner data, what consent sequencing, data-linking rules, and safety contingencies (unmatched reporting, emergency un-linking) will best protect participant confidentiality and safety?

response.query: If we add dyadic partner data, what consent sequencing, data-linking rules, and safety contingencies (unmatched reporting, emergency un-linking) will best protect participant confidentiality and safety?
response.answer: For dyadic partner data, ensure separate consent from each partner, use unique identifiers for linking, and have protocols for emergency un-linking and unmatched reporting to protect confidentiality and safety.

results.content: In 2000, the San Francisco VA Health Care System inaugurated a VA-funded Clinical Psychology Postdoctoral Residency (formerly Fellowship) Program in clinical psychology with two focus areas in Posttraumatic Stress Disorders (PTSD) and Substance Use Disorders (SUD). See also: https://profiles.ucsf.edu/jason.thompson Samuel Wan, PhD, has been Director of Training for the Clinical Psychology Postdoctoral Residency Training Program since 2014 and is Associate Chief of Mental Health for Education at the San Francisco VA Health Care System and Health Sciences Clinical Professor of Psychiatry at the School of Medicine at the University of California, San Francisco.
